name: InclusionBench
release_note: Provisional v0.4.0 for pull-request review; not a published release.
independence_policy: Separate metatheorem establishing neither ZFC proof of inclusion nor ZFC proof of its negation, unconditionally or conditional on Con(ZFC) or arithmetic soundness of ZFC. Arithmetic soundness means every first-order arithmetic sentence whose standard set-theoretic translation ZFC proves is true in the standard natural numbers. The exact premise must remain explicit in the proof, expert review and public result. No stronger unproved assumption is permitted. Independence does not enter ordinary relation closure.

independence_premises.unconditional: No additional consistency or soundness premise.
independence_premises.zfc_arithmetic_soundness: Every closed first-order arithmetic sentence whose standard translation is provable in ZFC is true in standard N.

classes.label: ACC⁰
classes.definition: Nonuniform polynomial-size, constant-depth AC⁰ circuits also allowing MOD_m gates for one fixed integer m ≥ 2; union over fixed moduli.

classes.label: TC⁰
classes.definition: Nonuniform polynomial-size, constant-depth circuits with unbounded-fan-in majority and Boolean gates.

classes.label: NC¹
classes.definition: Nonuniform polynomial-size Boolean circuits with bounded fan-in and O(log n) depth.

classes.label: L
classes.definition: Languages decided by deterministic machines using O(log n) work space and a read-only input tape.

classes.label: NL
classes.definition: Languages decided by nondeterministic machines using O(log n) work space; acceptance means some computation accepts.

classes.label: LogCFL
classes.definition: Languages logspace many-one reducible to a context-free language.

classes.label: uniform NC
classes.definition: Languages decided by logspace-uniform, polynomial-size bounded-fan-in Boolean circuit families with depth O((log n)^k) for some fixed k.

classes.label: SC
classes.definition: Languages decided by one deterministic machine in polynomial time and O((log n)^k) work space simultaneously, for some fixed k.

classes.label: P
classes.definition: Union over k of DTIME(n^k), under standard finite-alphabet multitape Turing-machine semantics.

classes.label: RP
classes.definition: Polynomial-time probabilistic decision algorithms with acceptance probability ≥ 1/2 on members and 0 on nonmembers.

classes.label: ZPP
classes.definition: Languages with zero-error randomized algorithms of expected polynomial running time; equivalently RP ∩ coRP.

classes.label: BPP
classes.definition: Polynomial-time probabilistic algorithms accepting members with probability ≥ 2/3 and nonmembers with probability ≤ 1/3.

classes.label: UP
classes.definition: Polynomial-time nondeterministic machines having at most one accepting computation per input.

classes.label: NP
classes.definition: Languages having polynomial-length binary witnesses checked by a deterministic polynomial-time verifier.

classes.label: coNP
classes.definition: Complements of NP languages.

classes.label: SPP
classes.definition: Languages whose characteristic function belongs to GapP: a polynomial-time nondeterministic machine has accepting-minus-rejecting gap 1 on members and 0 otherwise.

classes.label: C₌P
classes.definition: Languages L for which some GapP function g satisfies x ∈ L iff g(x) = 0. GapP functions are differences of #P functions.

classes.label: PP
classes.definition: Polynomial-time probabilistic algorithms whose acceptance probability is > 1/2 exactly on members; equivalently some GapP function is positive exactly on members.

classes.label: ⊕P
classes.definition: Languages recognized when a nondeterministic polynomial-time machine has an odd number of accepting computations.

classes.label: AWPP
classes.definition: For every polynomial r, there are g in GapP and a polynomial p with 0 ≤ g(x)/2^p(|x|) ≤ 1, at least 1−2^(−r(|x|)) on members and at most 2^(−r(|x|)) on nonmembers.

classes.label: MA
classes.definition: Total languages with polynomial-length classical proofs followed by a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier: some proof accepts members with probability ≥ 2/3, every proof accepts nonmembers with probability ≤ 1/3.

classes.label: AM
classes.definition: Total languages with a public-coin two-message protocol: Arthur sends polynomially many random bits, Merlin responds with a polynomial-length string, then a deterministic polynomial-time predicate decides; completeness ≥ 2/3, soundness ≤ 1/3.

classes.label: QCMA
classes.definition: Total languages verified by polynomial-time uniform quantum circuits and polynomial-length classical witnesses, with completeness ≥ 2/3 and soundness ≤ 1/3. Fix a standard finite universal algebraic gate set.

classes.label: QMA
classes.definition: Total languages verified by polynomial-time uniform quantum circuits and polynomial-qubit quantum witnesses, with completeness ≥ 2/3 and soundness ≤ 1/3. Fix a standard finite universal algebraic gate set.

classes.label: BQP
classes.definition: Total languages decided by polynomial-time uniform quantum circuits with error at most 1/3 on every input. Fix a standard finite universal algebraic gate set.

classes.label: SBP
classes.definition: There are f in #P and polynomial p such that f(x) ≥ 2^p(|x|) on members and f(x) ≤ 2^(p(|x|)−1) on nonmembers; #P counts accepting computations of nondeterministic polynomial-time machines.

classes.label: SZK
classes.definition: Total languages with an interactive statistical zero-knowledge proof: polynomial-time verifier, completeness ≥ 2/3 and soundness ≤ 1/3, and polynomial-time simulation of every efficient cheating verifier with negligible statistical error (auxiliary input allowed).

classes.label: NP ∩ coNP
classes.definition: Intersection of the language classes NP and coNP.

classes.label: Σ₂P
classes.definition: Languages expressible by a polynomial-time predicate with a polynomial-length existential witness followed by a polynomial-length universal witness; equivalently NP^NP.

classes.label: Δ₂P
classes.definition: P^NP: deterministic polynomial time with adaptive membership queries to an NP-complete language.

classes.label: Θ₂P
classes.definition: P^NP[O(log n)]: deterministic polynomial time with O(log n) adaptive queries to an NP-complete language; equivalently polynomially many nonadaptive queries.

classes.label: PH
classes.definition: Union of Σ_kP over fixed k ≥ 0, with Σ_0P=P and Σ_(k+1)P=NP^(Σ_kP).

classes.label: P/poly
classes.definition: Languages decided by deterministic polynomial-time machines with a polynomial-length advice string for each input length, with no computability requirement on advice; equivalently arbitrary polynomial-size Boolean circuit families.

classes.label: NP/poly
classes.definition: Languages decided by nondeterministic polynomial-time machines with arbitrary polynomial-length advice depending only on input length.

classes.label: PSPACE
classes.definition: Union over k of DSPACE(n^k).

classes.label: EXP
classes.definition: Union over k of DTIME(2^(n^k)).

classes.label: NEXP
classes.definition: Union over k of NTIME(2^(n^k)).

classes.label: EXPSPACE
classes.definition: Union over k of DSPACE(2^(n^k)).

classes.label: NE
classes.definition: Union over constants c of NTIME(2^(cn)).

classes.label: BPL
classes.definition: Languages decided with two-sided bounded error by one fair-coin machine with a polynomial worst-case running-time bound and logarithmic work space on every input and coin sequence. Input is read-only; random bits are fresh.

classes.label: UL
classes.definition: Languages recognized by a logarithmic-space nondeterministic machine with at most one accepting computation on every input; path multiplicity is counted. One polynomial clock bounds all branches.

classes.label: PL
classes.definition: Languages decided by an unbounded-error probabilistic logarithmic-space machine with a polynomial worst-case time bound: acceptance probability is strictly greater than one half exactly on members.

classes.label: BQL
classes.definition: Total languages decided with bounded error in polynomial time and logarithmic quantum and classical work space, with read-only classical input and space-bounded uniform control.

classes.label: ∃R
classes.definition: Polynomial-time many-one closure of the existential theory of the reals on finite binary encodings of formulas with integer coefficients. Quantified variables range over genuine real numbers; arbitrary real input constants and a polynomial-bit rational-witness restriction are excluded.

classes.label: P^#P
classes.definition: Deterministic polynomial time with adaptive access to one fixed PP oracle language; the established identity P^PP = P^#P names the same decision-language class. This is not the function class #P or the search class PPP.

classes.label: CH
classes.definition: The union of the fixed finite counting-hierarchy levels C_0=P and C_(k+1)=PP^(C_k), with one fixed oracle language for each machine. The level k is fixed independently of input length.

classes.label: QMA(2)
classes.definition: Total languages with a uniform polynomial-time quantum verifier receiving two unentangled polynomial-size quantum witnesses, with completeness at least 2/3 and soundness at most 1/3 on every input. Soundness quantifies over all product states across the two witness registers.

classes.label: StoqMA
classes.definition: Total-language stoquastic Merlin-Arthur verification using classical reversible gates, zero and plus ancillas and an X-basis output measurement. Take the union over uniformly polynomial-time computable rational completeness/soundness thresholds in [1/2,1] separated by an inverse polynomial; no general amplification or normalization to soundness 1/2 is assumed.

classes.label: QSZK
classes.definition: The total decision-language restriction of quantum statistical zero knowledge, specified through uniform quantum state-distinguishability circuits with the standard separated trace-distance thresholds and polynomial-time many-one reductions. The QSD characterization and threshold conventions are explicit trusted equivalence inputs.

classes.label: uniform NC¹
classes.definition: Standard DLOGTIME-uniform NC¹ using extended-connection (U_E) uniformity, equivalently alternating logarithmic time with random access to the input. Distinct from the nonuniform NC1 endpoint and from direct-connection-only U_D uniformity.

background_classes.label: AC⁰
background_classes.definition: Nonuniform polynomial-size, constant-depth Boolean circuits with unbounded-fan-in AND/OR and NOT gates.

background_classes.label: coRP
background_classes.definition: Complements of RP languages; polynomial-time algorithms accepting members with probability 1 and nonmembers with probability ≤ 1/2.

background_classes.label: FewP
background_classes.definition: Languages recognized by nondeterministic polynomial-time machines having at most polynomially many accepting computations on every input.

background_classes.label: LWPP
background_classes.definition: There are g in GapP and an integer-valued FP function f, nonzero on unary inputs, with g(x) = f(1^|x|) for members and g(x) = 0 for nonmembers.

background_classes.label: WPP
background_classes.definition: There are g in GapP and an integer-valued FP function f, nonzero on every input, with g(x) = f(x) for members and g(x) = 0 for nonmembers.

background_classes.label: coMA
background_classes.definition: Complements of total languages in MA.

background_classes.label: coAM
background_classes.definition: Complements of total languages in AM.

background_classes.label: coQMA
background_classes.definition: Complements of total languages in QMA.

background_classes.label: E
background_classes.definition: Union over constants c of DTIME(2^(cn)).

scenarios.title: What if BPP were strictly contained in NP?
scenarios.notes: Hypothetical result, not a verified achievement.

scenarios.title: What if P = NP?
scenarios.notes: Hypothetical result, not a verified achievement.

scenarios.title: P differs from NP
scenarios.notes: A language in NP requires superpolynomial deterministic time.

scenarios.title: Derandomize BPP in polynomial time
scenarios.notes: Full worst-case BPP=P, as total-language classes.

scenarios.title: Separate NP from coNP
scenarios.notes: The converse separation follows by complementation.

scenarios.title: Prove SAT has no bounded-error polynomial-time algorithm
scenarios.notes: SAT completeness transfers the lower bound to the class pair.

scenarios.title: Unconditional quantum advantage for a total decision language
scenarios.notes: Requires an unrelativized total language, not only a sampling or promise advantage.

scenarios.title: Rule out polynomial-time quantum algorithms for NP-complete problems
scenarios.notes: Requires an unconditional complexity lower bound.

scenarios.title: A total BQP language outside the polynomial hierarchy
scenarios.notes: An oracle separation does not suffice.

scenarios.title: A total QMA language with no QCMA verifier
scenarios.notes: This expressly requires a total language; the promise-only version is separately listed as unsupported.

scenarios.title: Simulate quantum witnesses with classical witnesses
scenarios.notes: A full promise-QMA containment also implies this total-language containment.

scenarios.title: Remove witnesses from all quantum NP verification
scenarios.notes: A full promise collapse gives the stated total-language consequence.

scenarios.title: Classical bounded-error algorithms for all statistical zero knowledge
scenarios.notes: A full promise-SZK collapse is strong enough; algorithms for individual problems are not.

scenarios.title: A total statistical zero-knowledge language outside BQP
scenarios.notes: Must produce a total-language separation.

scenarios.title: Derandomize Merlin–Arthur verification
scenarios.notes: Direct verifier-class collapse; total BPP=P alone is not imported as a proof.

scenarios.title: Derandomize Arthur–Merlin verification
scenarios.notes: Removes public randomness from the two-message proof class.

scenarios.title: Prove the polynomial hierarchy extends beyond its second level
scenarios.notes: A separation of any higher PH level from Sigma2P suffices.

scenarios.title: Separate polynomial space from the polynomial hierarchy
scenarios.notes: An unconditional PSPACE language outside PH.

scenarios.title: Separate polynomial time from polynomial space
scenarios.notes: Could follow from any intermediate separation between P and PSPACE.

scenarios.title: Separate deterministic exponential time from polynomial space
scenarios.notes: Distinguishes the two union classes, not a fixed resource bound.

scenarios.title: Separate nondeterministic and deterministic exponential time
scenarios.notes: Requires separation of the union classes; an E-versus-NE separation alone has different strength.

scenarios.title: Deterministic logspace directed reachability
scenarios.notes: An L algorithm for directed s-t connectivity gives L=NL.

scenarios.title: Prove polynomial-time computation cannot all be parallelized
scenarios.notes: NC is logspace-uniform polylog-depth polynomial-size circuits.

scenarios.title: Separate logarithmic-depth circuits from constant-depth threshold circuits
scenarios.notes: Both circuit classes in this comparison are nonuniform.

scenarios.title: Separate threshold circuits from constant-depth modular circuits
scenarios.notes: Both classes allow arbitrary nonuniform polynomial-size families.

scenarios.title: Superpolynomial threshold-circuit lower bounds for NEXP
scenarios.notes: Must hold against all fixed depths and all polynomial sizes, not just depth two or one fixed size exponent.

scenarios.title: Superpolynomial general circuit lower bounds for NP
scenarios.notes: An NP language without polynomial-size Boolean circuits.

scenarios.title: Superpolynomial general circuit lower bounds for NEXP
scenarios.notes: A weaker target class than NP, but still a major unresolved general-circuit barrier.

scenarios.title: Superpolynomial general circuit lower bounds for PSPACE
scenarios.notes: Fixed-exponent lower bounds with a different hard language for each exponent do not establish this.

scenarios.title: One PP language requiring superpolynomial-size circuits
scenarios.notes: Must exchange the quantifiers in known fixed-exponent PP lower bounds: one language defeats all polynomial exponents.

scenarios.title: Separate parity counting from deterministic polynomial time
scenarios.notes: A total parity-counting language without a P algorithm.

scenarios.title: Prove quantum computers cannot decide every PP language efficiently
scenarios.notes: A total-language lower bound for quantum computation.

scenarios.title: Separate unambiguous nondeterminism from deterministic time
scenarios.notes: A total language with an unambiguous polynomial verifier but no P algorithm.

scenarios.title: Prove efficient certificates on both sides do not imply easy decision
scenarios.notes: A total NP intersect coNP language outside P.

scenarios.title: Separate NP from unambiguous polynomial time
scenarios.notes: Rules out UP verifiers for at least one NP language.

scenarios.title: Quantum algorithms for every SPP language
scenarios.notes: A whole-class simulation, not only a graph-isomorphism algorithm.

scenarios.title: Match quantum computation to its AWPP counting upper bound
scenarios.notes: Since BQP is already contained in AWPP, this would establish equality.

scenarios.title: Polynomial-time algorithms for every TFNP search problem
scenarios.notes: For any L in NP intersect coNP, ask for either an NP certificate of membership or a coNP certificate of nonmembership, tagged with its side. This is a total polynomially bounded NP search relation. A polynomial solver decides L. This argument does not apply to a collapse of PPAD alone.

scenarios.title: Derandomize polynomial-time logarithmic-space computation
scenarios.notes: BPL keeps both a logarithmic workspace bound and a polynomial worst-case clock. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Make logarithmic-space nondeterminism unambiguous
scenarios.notes: UL permits at most one accepting path on every input. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Deterministically simulate every unambiguous logspace language
scenarios.notes: This does not assume a solution to a promise-only unique-path problem. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Turn unbounded-error logspace computation into bounded-error computation
scenarios.notes: Both endpoints have polynomial clocks; the error gap is the distinction. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Classically simulate bounded-error quantum logspace
scenarios.notes: The quantum computation has logarithmic workspace and polynomial running time. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Match quantum logspace to its unbounded-error counting upper bound
scenarios.notes: An unbounded-time quantum simulation does not establish this polynomial-time inclusion. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Simulate all deterministic logspace languages in uniform logarithmic depth
scenarios.notes: UniformNC1 uses standard extended-connection uniformity, equivalently ALOGTIME. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Simulate uniform logarithmic depth by constant-depth threshold circuits
scenarios.notes: The target TC0 is nonuniform. This hypothesis is distinct from silently treating NC1 as uniform. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Give ordinary NP certificates for real feasibility
scenarios.notes: The inputs are finite binary descriptions; real assignments need not have short rational encodings. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Place real feasibility in the counting hierarchy
scenarios.notes: CH is a union of fixed finite levels, not a hierarchy whose level grows with input length. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Solve every real-feasibility language with bounded-error quantum computation
scenarios.notes: This concerns the total binary decision class, not real-input BSS computation. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Eliminate deterministic adaptive PP-oracle queries
scenarios.notes: PSharpP is the decision class P^PP=P^#P. This alone is not encoded as a collapse of CH. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Collapse the counting hierarchy to deterministic counting-oracle computation
scenarios.notes: The reverse containment is in the baseline. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Place polynomial space in the counting hierarchy
scenarios.notes: The reverse containment is in the baseline. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Remove the extra power of two unentangled quantum proofs
scenarios.notes: The witnesses are unentangled across the two proof registers. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Simulate two unentangled quantum proofs in polynomial space
scenarios.notes: The ordinary baseline upper bound is NEXP, not PSPACE. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Verify nondeterministic exponential time with two unentangled proofs
scenarios.notes: The total NEXP endpoint has the standard total-completion interpretation discussed in the roster dossier. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Classically simulate stoquastic quantum verification
scenarios.notes: StoqMA uses the standard inverse-polynomial-gap threshold union; it is not the NP slice with soundness exactly one half. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Remove interaction from quantum statistical zero knowledge
scenarios.notes: Every input must satisfy the gap; a promise-only theorem needs a valid total-language transfer. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

scenarios.title: Give quantum witnesses for all quantum statistical zero-knowledge languages
scenarios.notes: No unconditional QSZK⊆QMA or QSZK⊆PP is imported merely from a common PSPACE upper bound. Hypothetical result, not a verified model achievement.

sources.notes: Fenner, Fortnow and Kurtz. Author PDF https://cse.sc.edu/~fenner/papers/gaps.pdf has poor extracted text; readable definitions and inclusion chain also checked in q-ffkl02.

sources.title: An Oracle Builder's Toolkit
sources.locator: Section 2.1, Definition 2.3, printed pp. 5–6; Section 6.1, Definition 6.2 and Lemma 6.3
sources.notes: Fenner, Fortnow, Kurtz and Li. PDF dated 2002-11-11; expanded version of 1993 conference paper. Gives readable counting definitions, FewP–SPP–LWPP–WPP–C=P–PP chain and WPP contained in AWPP.

sources.title: Small Bounded-Error Computations and Completeness
sources.locator: Abstract; Section 1; Definition 2.9; Proposition 3.3; Section 4
sources.notes: Böhler, Glaßer and Meister. Primary authors' paper states MA contained in SBP contained in AM intersect BPPpath and BPPpath contained in PP; language-level gap definitions are explicit.

sources.title: Honest-Verifier Statistical Zero-Knowledge Equals General Statistical Zero-Knowledge
sources.locator: Section 1, especially printed pp. 1–2: HVSZK contained in AM intersect coAM; HVSZK closed under complement; theorem HVSZK=SZK
sources.notes: Goldreich, Sahai and Vadhan. For AM upper bound authors credit Fortnow and Aiello–Håstad; for complement closure Okamoto and Sahai–Vadhan. Total-language restrictions inherit both conclusions.

sources.title: Can Statistical Zero Knowledge be Made Non-Interactive? or On the Relationship of SZK and NISZK
sources.locator: Theorems 1.5–1.6; explicit warning immediately after Theorem 1.5
sources.notes: Goldreich, Sahai and Vadhan. SZK=BPP iff NISZK=BPP here is explicitly about promise problems. Do not import it as an implication about total-language classes without an additional argument. NISZK is outside the final roster.

sources.title: BPP and the Polynomial Hierarchy
sources.locator: Abstract / main theorem
sources.notes: Lautemann's primary publication proves BPP contained in Sigma2P; complement closure also gives Pi2P.

sources.title: In Search of an Easy Witness: Exponential Time vs. Probabilistic Polynomial Time
sources.locator: Main equivalence NEXP contained in P/poly iff NEXP=MA; full journal manuscript Section 4.1
sources.notes: Impagliazzo, Kabanets and Wigderson; JCSS 65(4), 672–694, 2002; preliminary CCC 2001. Full theorem checked at https://www.math.tau.ac.il/~amnon/Classes/2017-BPP/Lectures/IKW02.pdf (abstract and Section 4.1).

sources.title: Algebrization: A New Barrier in Complexity Theory
sources.locator: Theorem 3.5 and paragraph immediately following, printed p. 12; Corollary 3.15; Section 3.5
sources.notes: Aaronson and Wigderson. Taking trivial oracles gives PP contained in P/poly implies P^#P contained in MA. Restricting to PP yields the roster rule; Toda also yields PH contained in MA.

sources.title: Separating QMA from QCMA with a Classical Oracle
sources.locator: Abstract / main theorem
sources.notes: Bostanci, Haferkamp, Nirkhe and Zhandry. Published before the benchmark cutoff. This is an oracle separation and is deliberately NOT a QMA-versus-QCMA baseline fact.

sources.title: Non-Uniform ACC Circuit Lower Bounds
sources.locator: Abstract / main theorem
sources.notes: Williams. Journal of the ACM, 2014, DOI 10.1145/2559903; preliminary result 2011. Theorem 1.1 strengthens NEXP to NTIME[2^n]. Source ID is stable despite the bibliographic correction.

sources.title: Derandomizing Polynomial Identity Tests Means Proving Circuit Lower Bounds
sources.locator: Authors' abstract, first and second paragraphs
sources.notes: Kabanets and Impagliazzo. The consequence of BPP=P is a DISJUNCTION involving arithmetic permanent lower bounds, not the unconditional Boolean statement NEXP not contained in P/poly.

sources.title: A Complete Problem for Statistical Zero Knowledge
sources.locator: Theorem 3.1, page 208; Section 3.2 polarization lemma
sources.notes: Primary source for the Statistical Difference characterization used by the optional operational SZK definition. The characterization equivalence is not proved in this repository.

sources.title: Gap-definable Counting Classes
sources.authors: Stephen Fenner, Lance Fortnow, Stuart Kurtz
sources.locator: Sections 3–5, especially Theorem 5.5; original PDF extraction is degraded
sources.notes: Original source for GapP classes, FewP inclusion and lowness. Corroborated with KST1992 and STT2005, which explicitly identify the inherited theorem.
sources.round2_access: Primary author manuscript downloaded and visually read at printed pp.17–19: Corollary5.8; Definition5.13 and subsequent LWPP lowness/Turing-closure discussion.

sources.title: An Oracle Builder’s Toolkit
sources.authors: Stephen Fenner, Lance Fortnow, Stuart Kurtz, Lide Li
sources.locator: Definition 2.2, Definition 2.3; Definition 6.1, Lemma 6.3 and Corollary 6.4, printed pp.25–26

sources.round2_access: primary text independently reopened; theorem locators verified

sources.title: Graph Isomorphism is Low for PP
sources.authors: Johannes Köbler, Uwe Schöning, Jacobo Torán
sources.locator: Section 2.2, printed p.8, Theorem 2.9 and paragraph after Definition 2.10

sources.title: A Complexity Theory for Feasible Closure Properties
sources.locator: Propositions 2.6(5), 2.7(2–3), printed pp.7–8; Theorem 3.2 and first proof bullet, pp.10–11
sources.notes: Primary technical report; journal version JCSS46(3),1993. Theorem3.2(3) is PP=UP; (4) also equates PH, CH, CeqP, PP and parityP with UP. Prop2.7(2): PP⊆C=·CeqP. Prop2.7(3): parityP^parityP=P^parityP=parityP.
sources.round2_access: primary text independently reopened; theorem locators verified

sources.title: Quantum and Classical Complexity Classes: Separations, Collapses, and Closure Properties
sources.authors: Holger Spakowski, Mayur Thakur, Rahul Tripathi
sources.locator: Theorem5.1 (PH⊆UP^CeqP), Theorem5.4(a), Theorem5.6(a,b), Theorem5.9; journal pp.24–28. Introduction attributes SPP^LWPP=LWPP to FFK94.
sources.notes: Primary manuscript OCR is corrupt; exact statements verified also in indexed full journal PDF: https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d52acf5cae7e117a88744fa578719a97afc7e26d&repid=rep1&type=pdf . WPP truth-table closure; UP^WPP⊆coCeqP. Oracle failures are not ordinary separations.
sources.round2_access: Primary manuscript downloaded and visually read at printed pp.3,22–24; PDF text font mapping is corrupted. Journal metadata independently confirms July 2005; manuscript locators differ from journal pagination.

sources.title: QMA=PP implies that PP contains PH
sources.locator: Theorem1 pp.5–6; Theorem2 pp.7–8; Corollaries1–2 p.8
sources.quote: If QMA = PP then QMA = PP ⊇ PH.
sources.notes: Corollary 2 assumes coCeqP=PP. The weaker CeqP⊆QMA premise is supplied by explicit derivation D2 in the audit, independently checked by two reviewers; it is not quoted as a named theorem from this paper.
sources.round2_access: primary text independently reopened; theorem locators verified

sources.title: Quantum Arthur–Merlin Games
sources.locator: Definition of QMA; Theorem3.3 amplification, Theorem3.4 and Remark3.5, pp.13–14
sources.notes: Also QMA⊆A0PP. Bounded-error total languages are obtained by requiring the verifier gap on every input.
sources.round2_access: primary text independently reopened; theorem locators verified

sources.title: Complexity Limitations on Quantum Computation
sources.locator: Definition2.1 and following paragraph, p.3; Theorem3.1, Theorem3.3, Corollaries3.4–3.5, pp.5–7
sources.quote: BQP machines can simulate deterministic Turing machines and other BQP machines as subroutines
sources.notes: BQP⊆AWPP and AWPP is PP-low. The subroutine paragraph cites Bernstein–Vazirani1997. Classical adaptive-query simulation needs only amplification and polynomial composition.
sources.round2_access: primary text independently reopened; theorem locators verified

sources.title: Quantum Complexity Theory
sources.locator: Sections4–7 composition/simulation, Section8.1 amplification and inclusion bounds, Section8.3 quantum oracles
sources.notes: Primary journal paper at an academic mirror; verifies finite precision, machine/circuit robustness, and efficient composition.
sources.round2_access: Composition result used via Fortnow–Rogers explicit primary statement; full BV proof not reread in this round.

sources.title: PP is as Hard as the Polynomial-Time Hierarchy
sources.locator: Abstract and main theorem, SIAM J.Comput.20(5),865–877
sources.notes: Also PH⊆P^PP. BP denotes bounded-error randomized reduction, not an assertion PH⊆parityP or PH⊆PP.
sources.round2_access: Publisher abstract directly states PH⊆P^PP and PH⊆BP·parityP. Strong one-#P-query version read in STT Theorem5.1 proof and Vyalyi Theorem2 proof.

sources.title: The Size of SPP
sources.locator: Theorem2.1 p.2; paragraph before Corollary5.3 pp.5–6

sources.round2_access: primary text independently reopened; theorem locators verified

sources.title: RL ⊆ SC

sources.notes: ECCC TR96-013; journal SIAM J.Comput.27(5),1430–1437 (1998), DOI10.1137/S0097539795295924. PL^PL=PL here uses RST relativization; it is not an unrestricted oracle theorem.

sources.title: Making Nondeterminism Unambiguous
sources.locator: Introduction and §2; Theorem2.2 and Corollary2.3
sources.notes: Author manuscript; SIAM J.Comput.29(4),1118–1131(2000), DOI10.1137/S0097539798339041. NL⊆UL/poly does not remove advice.

sources.locator: Theorems1.2,3.3,3.6,3.9–3.13; §5 open questions

sources.locator: Theorems1–2, Corollary3, Theorem4 and definitions in §2

coverage.status: coverage stress test; not a ranked forecast and not an exhaustive set of likely advances
coverage.population: 50 concrete structural or algorithmic breakthrough scenarios selected to probe coverage. Opposite answers to one open question are not systematically counted twice.
coverage.interpretation: Direct and consequence mean that a mathematical mapping is provided, conditional on the mapped pair being certified open at the cutoff. They do not certify that the result was still open or guarantee an official score in the draft benchmark. Unsupported means no scored implication is established here, not that no implication could ever exist.

scenarios.title: Polynomial-time algorithms for every TFNP search problem
scenarios.notes: For any L in NP intersect coNP, ask for either an NP certificate of membership or a coNP certificate of nonmembership, tagged with its side. This is a total polynomially bounded NP search relation. A polynomial solver decides L. This argument does not apply to a collapse of PPAD alone.
scenarios.eligibility: pending cutoff certification; direct reduction argument supplied

scenarios.title: Polynomial-time graph isomorphism
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A faster algorithm for this individual language does not imply that NP, SPP or any other roster class collapses. GI is not known complete for those classes.

scenarios.title: Classical polynomial-time integer factoring
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Factoring is a particular search/function problem. Its efficient solution need not decide every language in NP intersect coNP or BQP.

scenarios.title: Deterministic polynomial-time general polynomial identity testing
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Known implications include a disjunction: NEXP lacks polynomial-size Boolean circuits OR permanent lacks polynomial-size arithmetic circuits. The second branch need not settle a roster pair.

scenarios.title: Prove the matrix multiplication exponent is two
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: All the algorithms involved remain polynomial time; the roster has no fixed-exponent arithmetic-operation classes.

scenarios.title: Refute SETH with a faster exponential-time SAT algorithm
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A speedup can refute a quantitative hypothesis while leaving P versus NP and all roster inclusions unresolved. A proof of ETH or SETH would imply NP not contained in P, but refutation need not.

scenarios.title: Truly subquadratic exact edit distance
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: This distinguishes polynomial exponents inside P. Without a separate theorem connecting the speedup to a roster relation, the benchmark awards no point.

scenarios.title: Polynomial-time algorithms for every PPAD search problem
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: PPAD is a class of total search relations, outside this language roster. Solving PPAD-complete Nash problems need not settle any listed language inclusion.

scenarios.title: Separate VP from VNP over characteristic zero
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Algebraic circuit families are not Boolean decision-language classes. No implication to a scored Boolean pair is supplied by this benchmark.

scenarios.title: Superpolynomial lower bounds for Frege proofs
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Lower bounds for one proof system do not by themselves establish NP differs from coNP; that conclusion requires ruling out every polynomially bounded Cook–Reckhow proof system.

scenarios.title: Prove the Hamiltonian quantum PCP conjecture
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A gap-amplification/completeness result can be a major advance without changing a total-language class inclusion.

scenarios.title: Separate promise-QMA from promise-QCMA without a total-language witness
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A promise-problem witness does not automatically produce a total language in QMA outside QCMA. The corresponding total-language scenario is advance-08.

scenarios.title: A new separation relative to an oracle
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: The scorer fixes unrelativized classes. Even a major new oracle separation does not prove their unrelativized noninclusion. The classical-oracle QMA/QCMA problem was already solved before the cutoff.

scenarios.title: A superlinear or fixed-exponent Boolean circuit lower bound for an explicit NP language
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Ruling out n^1.01-size circuits leaves n^2-size circuits possible and does not give NP not contained in P/poly. Likewise fixed-depth threshold bounds do not settle NEXP versus TC0.

scenarios.title: Optimal explicit Ramsey graph constructions
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A construction for one combinatorial object need not derandomize all BPP languages or resolve any roster pair. Whole-class consequences would need their own proof.

gaps: Individual algorithms versus whole complexity classes
Fixed resource exponents and fine-grained complexity

A finite sample cannot support a claim to cover the 50 most likely advances without a separately elicited and versioned forecast distribution.

roster_recommendation.accepted_choice: Provisional v0.4.0 uses50 scored classes and61 context classes. The eleven additions and eleven demotions are documented in research/v0.4.0/roster-decision.md. UniformNC1 is separate from nonuniform NC1; NC remains logspace-uniform.
roster_recommendation.benefit: The revised roster adds small-space randomness and counting, unambiguity, quantum logspace, real feasibility, counting-oracle computation and CH, two unentangled proofs, stoquastic verification and quantum zero knowledge.
roster_recommendation.tradeoff: Eleven previous endpoints become background proof vocabulary. Some positive collapses, and direct independence results involving those endpoints, can lose credit. The loss audit is explicit; complements are not treated as interchangeable aliases.
possible_future_tracks: Fixed-exponent circuit, time and proof-size targets
